question: Why does Laya, flying by command, fail to follow the 4x rover that the lookahead teacher follows, and what fixes it?

hypotheses.H1: Perception: from one 512x384 frame Laya cannot localise the rover (bearing, range) precisely enough to steer at 4x.
hypotheses.H2: Control: a held absolute heading, the 120 deg/s yaw-rate cap and 4-7 Hz commands cannot track the 4x rover even with right decisions.
hypotheses.H3: Covariate shift: small early errors take Laya to states the teacher never visited, where it has no data and cannot recover (DAgger's case).
hypotheses.H4: Under-training: the imitation is not converged (60% top-1, still rising); more steps or data on the same targets would fix it.
hypotheses.H5: Partial observability: the teacher's choice depends on privileged information (where the rover will be, the map round corners) that one frame + lidar + speed does not contain, so no student can match it from these inputs.
hypotheses.H6: Latency: answers arrive too late (0.1 s compute, up to 0.6 s freshness) for a 4x rover.
hypotheses.H7: Action parameterisation: independent marginals over speed / slide / turn and coarse levels (turn +-20/45/90 deg) cannot express the teacher's joint choice.
hypotheses.H8: Train/deploy mismatch: the inputs at flight time differ from the recorded training inputs (frame, context keys or semantics, lidar), a bug.
hypotheses.H9: Causal confusion (copycat): the context carries the previous command (prev_speed, prev_turn), which in the teacher's data predicts its next choice well; the student learned to lean on it, and in flight its own lagging commands feed back into it (de Haan et al. 2019, 'Causal Confusion in Imitation Learning'; Wen et al. 2020, 'Fighting Copycat Agents').
hypotheses.H10: Overfitting: the student memorised the training flights and seeds and does not generalise to new ones.

evidence.text: Teacher, deciding at 4 Hz from privileged state but holding the decided heading between decisions (bestfix), follows the 4x rover 16/16; with blurred T=5 targets decoded (softfix:5) 20/20.
evidence.note: Held heading + yaw cap + 4 Hz suffice given right decisions (against H2); commands snapped to the command levels still fly (against H7; the turn is continuous in bestfix, so H7 only partly). 0.25 s decisions with no latency: weakly against H6.

evidence.text: Student-vs-teacher diagnostic, paused sim time (no latency): v3.6 fails as in wall clock (rover in view 15-29%, 2-5 hits per 25 s).
v3.6 in its first 3 s (rover in view 100%, states the teacher recorded from): speed 5.0-5.5 vs teacher 5.3-6.3, heading off by 11-32 deg (median), slide 0.2-1.2 vs 1.2-1.8; regret 1-4.
evidence.note: Errors already present before any drift: against covariate shift as the ROOT cause (it can still compound them).

evidence.text: After ~3 s v3.6 loses the rover (in view 15-55%) and regret grows; heading lags the teacher's turn into corners (-13 vs -36 deg).
Sharp targets (v3.6) vs blurred (v3.5): first-3-s speed 2.5-3.4 -> 5.0-5.5, heading error ~33 -> 11-32 deg, held-out top-1 52% -> 60% (still rising at the end).
evidence.note: The student tracks what its targets say, so its inputs do carry the signal it trained on: weakly against a gross mismatch bug.

evidence.text: Four iterations of outcome-reward RL (90 sampled flights each) from v3.6: return 11.3, 10.1, 14.3, 9.9; rover in view 16-20%; held-out teacher NLL 1.0 -> 2.1.
evidence.note: Weak: sparse, noisy RL failing is consistent with most hypotheses; it fits a cause no amount of training on these inputs removes.

evidence.text: At 1x, Laya v3.3 steering the pursuit from its perception (visible/bearing answers) followed the rover 38/48 in wall clock and town 6/6.
evidence.note: Laya localised the rover well enough at 1x from one frame; 4x needs more precision and anticipation, so only weakly against H1.

evidence.text: X1 audit: flight and training build the same context keys in the same order, same Eye, 512x384 frame, same turn convention; only differences: training frames were JPEG q90, flight frames raw, and prev_speed/prev_turn are the teacher's previous choice in training but the student's own in flight. In the teacher's held-out data, copying prev_turn gets the turn level right 49% (majority 21%), prev_speed the speed 65% (majority 43%); corr 0.77 / 0.68.
evidence.note: No bug-level mismatch (against H8). The copy-the-previous-command baseline nearly equals the student's 60% top-1: the shortcut is available and strong.

evidence.text: X6 copycat probe (v3.6, 600 held-out teacher decisions): turn top-1 56.5% with the recorded previous command, 35.8% with a random other decision's, 35.0% with zeros; speed 66.7 -> 47.7 / 46.5; slide (no previous value in the context) 71.3 -> 68.2 / 68.5. With a foreign previous command the answer still tracks it (corr 0.56 turn, 0.63 speed). Image-only competence: turn 35% (majority 21%), speed 47% (majority 43%).
evidence.note: Direct test of H9: the student leans on the previous command and follows it even when it is unrelated to the frame. The image-only skill left over is weak, which is also what H1 and H5 predict, so they stay open.

evidence.text: X7 intervention: v3.7 trained without the previous command in its context. Held-out mean top-1 54.9% (v3.6 image-only ~51%, with its shortcut 60%). Diagnostic vs v3.6: rover in view 33% vs 21%, hits 15 vs 20; 3-8 s in view 39% vs 32%, regret 3.0 vs 5.0; 8-25 s in view 20% vs 4%, regret 0.4 vs 2.4; but 0-3 s heading error 31 vs 17 deg. One flight (town-x4 seed 1) kept the rover in view 97% with no hit.
evidence.note: Removing the shortcut helps after the start (H9 is a real contributor, as predicted) but is not a fix; without the crutch the early steering is worse: the image-only skill is weak (H1 or H4). H5 predicted no flight gain: mildly against.

evidence.text: v3.6 top-1 on teacher decisions it trained on 65.5% vs held-out flights 59.7% (a 6-point gap); held-out teacher data keeps the previous-command shortcut (56.5% turn with it), so validation cannot see the shortcut, which breaks only when the previous command becomes the student's own.
evidence.source: v3.6 training log (train_eval vs val); X6
evidence.note: Small generalisation gap: not memorisation. The failure is a shortcut that holds in train and validation alike.

experiments.cost: CPU dataset + 1 A100-hour training + 6 GPU diagnostic flights
experiments.what: Keep the previous command but drop it out: retrain from v3.4/best on teacher_sharp where each record's prev_speed/prev_turn is replaced by 0/0 with probability 0.5 (ChauffeurNet's past-motion dropout; Wen et al. 2020), then the diagnostic WITH the previous command (the student's own) and the copycat probe.

predictions.H9: copycat probe: small gap between recorded and foreign previous command; diagnostic at least as good as v3.7 after 3 s and better than v3.7 in the first 3 s (smoothness back without the crutch)
predictions.H1: image-only top-1 stays ~35% turn; early steering no better than v3.7

experiments.what: Audit train vs deploy inputs: for the same simulator state, build the context and frame the way teacher.fly(record=True) recorded them and the way teacher.diagnose / run.py flight feed them; diff state_text keys and values (prev_turn sign and units, lidar sector order, travel_deg), image size, JPEG vs raw, camera pose.

Copycat probe: v3.6 answers 600 held-out teacher decisions (drone_rover_teacher_sharp val) three ways: recorded prev_speed/prev_turn; prev replaced by those of a random other decision; prev set to 0. Measure top-1 vs the teacher and how far the answer follows the injected prev.

predictions.H9: accuracy drops sharply with shuffled prev (toward the image-only level) and answers track the injected prev
predictions.H1: small drop; answers follow the image

experiments.cost: CPU dataset + 1 A100-hour training + 6 GPU diagnostic flights
experiments.what: Retrain from v3.4/best on drone_rover_teacher_sharp with prev_speed/prev_turn removed from the context (drone_rover_teacher_sharp_noprev), same mix and schedule as v3.6 (run drone-rover-v3.7-noprev); then the student-vs-teacher diagnostic (keys without prev) and compare with v3.6.

predictions.H9: held-out turn top-1 clearly above v3.6's image-only 35% (the model now has to learn from the frame); diagnostic: rover in view and heading error after 3 s clearly better than v3.6, since there is no feedback of its own lag
predictions.H5: held-out top-1 stays near 35% turn / 47% speed; no flight gain
predictions.H1: same as H5 at this resolution; X3/X4 separate them
predictions.H4: a modest rise, with or without prev

experiments.what: Teacher with commands quantised exactly as the student outputs them (speed/slide/turn snapped to the levels, turn relative to the nose at decision time, held) on the six 4x courses x 4 seeds.
Oracle-heading hybrid: v3.6 flies in the teacher's world with its own speed and slide but the turn replaced by the teacher's (and, separately, speed/slide from the teacher and turn from Laya).

predictions.H1: oracle turn fixes most failures; Laya's turn with oracle speed/slide still fails
predictions.H5: same as H1 (the turn needs privileged anticipation)
predictions.H3: oracle turn helps early but drift errors in speed/slide still accumulate

experiments.what: Observability check: teacher flights (six 4x courses x seeds 20-23) log per decision the TRUE observable features (rover visible, bearing, range, speed, travel, altitude, lidar), the same plus the two previous decisions' observations (memory), and the same plus privileged ones (the rover 1-3 s ahead in the drone's frame, its velocity); softmax regression and kNN predict the teacher's turn / speed / slide level, held out by seed (autoresearch/x4_fit.py).

predictions.H5: obs+priv predicts the turn far better than obs (the choice needs the future); memory helps only partly
predictions.H1: true obs already predicts the turn well above Laya's image-only 35% (so the information is in the observation and Laya's perception is what falls short)
predictions.H4: as H1 (the signal is there; more training should find it)

experiments.cost: GPU, one DAgger round (~2 h collect + 1 h train)
experiments.what: One DAgger round: v3.6 flies, the teacher labels every state (sharp targets), retrain, re-run the diagnostic.

predictions.H3: later-seconds regret falls clearly, rover in view rises
predictions.H5: little gain: labels at the new states are equally unpredictable from the inputs

conclusions.summary: H9 (copycat through the previous command) is real: removing it (X7) raised rover-in-view after the start from 4% to 20% (8-25 s) and cut collisions, but the student's steering from the image alone is still weak (early heading error 31 deg). The open question is whether the image carries what the teacher decides on (H1 perception / H4 training) or not (H5 observability): X4 fits the teacher's choices from true observable vs privileged features.
milestones: X6: if the student's accuracy collapses with shuffled prev_* and its answers track it, retrain without prev_* (or with it dropped out) as the intervention
X3/X4 still split perception from observability
